title: Midnight Flagfall — Quick Runbook & Handoff Notes
content:
TL;DR:
- This is a compact, two-page style quickrun for the midnight shift (Flagfall). Not a replacement for the canonical runbooks — use this for immediate triage and temporary patching until morning rotation.

Shift goals:
- Keep latency SLOs within targets for hosted inference endpoints (p50 < 80ms, p95 < 350ms).
- Contain and mitigate any bursty KV-cache evictions causing regen storms.
- Avoid model rollbacks unless a verified quality regression.

Active watchlist (current):
- hosted/text-gen-prod-v2: increased 5xxs since 02:13 UTC — likely autoscaler thrash.
- kv-cache-hotshot: prefix-hit rate dropped from 88% -> 46% after 01:40 UTC.
- dedicated/gpu-pool-3: one node (node-3a) reported GPU ECC warnings last week; monitor thermal alerts.

Immediate triage checklist (what I do first):
1) Open live dashboards: Console -> Routes -> hosted/text-gen-prod-v2 (look at per-token latency heatmap, error rate).
2) Check autoscale events: infra -> scaling-events -> filter route=text-gen-prod-v2 -> last 6 hours.
3) Check node health: sops -> nodes -> node-3a telemetry (GPU temp, driver reboots).
4) Verify KV cache metrics: optimize -> cache-metrics -> prefix-hit / miss ratio and last eviction timestamp.
5) If error spike correlated with scale events, flip route to fallback variant (text-gen-prod-v2-fallback) for up to 30m:
   - Command: curl -X POST "$REDWOOD_CONSOLE/api/v1/routes/switch" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"hosted/text-gen-prod-v2","target":"hosted/text-gen-prod-v2-fallback","duration_min":30}'
   - Note: inform customer-success/channel (#prod-alerts) if this will affect model outputs.

Quick mitigation steps (order of preference):
- If KV cache hit rate low and mem pressure high: temporarily disable aggressive prefix eviction policy for affected pool.
  - Console -> Optimize -> Caching -> pool=kv-cache-hotshot -> set eviction_policy=LRU-ttl-extended (increase TTL by +30s)
- If autoscaler thrash suspected: bump stabilization window to 120s for that route, reduce scaling step-down.
  - infra -> autoscaler-config -> route=text-gen-prod-v2 -> stabilizationSeconds=120
- If a single node is noisy: cordon node-3a and drain non-critical pods; if GPU errors persist, emergency-replace with node-3b.
  - k8s: kubectl cordon node-3a && kubectl drain node-3a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

Escalation contacts (order):
- On-call SRE (primary): Aisha Patel (pager) — 30 min response expectation
- Serving runtime lead: Marco Silva (slack) — 1 hour
- Infra hardware specialist: Priya Narayanan (email/pager) — for hardware replacement
- Customer-impacting incident (P1): page exec-oncall and eng-lead, create JIRA and tag "incident"

Recent incident notes (for handoff):
- 2026-02-24 23:50 UTC: regen storm on reranking-route after cache eviction policy update. Root cause: a background job invalidated hot prefixes unexpectedly. Mitigation deployed: temporary TTL increase + rewarm job.
- Action items carried: verify rewarm job success (see linked artifact: JIRA-OPS-4312).

Commands I use often (copy/paste-ready):
- Check route logs (last 100 lines): kubectl logs -n redwood svc/text-gen-prod-v2 --tail=100
- Get autoscale events: gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.route_id="text-gen-prod-v2"' --freshness=6h --limit=50
- Switch to fallback variant (see above curl) — keep transcript in #prod-alerts with timestamp.

Notes to self (things I scribble while triaging):
- If switching to fallback, watch dkim/regression tests for 15 minutes. If we see quality drop, revert and open postmortem.
- Avoid full rollback to older model build x.10 unless 3+ independent signals show regression.
- When draining node, watch for pending queue growth on dedicated pools; increase burst capacity if queue > 200 reqs.

Parking lot / follow-ups for morning crew:
- Revisit prefix invalidation job: add TTL sanity checks and a dry-run mode. (Owner: solutions-eng -> PR #629)
- Add synthetic tests for HTTP 5xx spike simulation to validate autoscaler configs.
- Replace node-3a NVMe (warranty claim) — escalate to infra ops.

Open questions (need PM/eng review):
- Should fallback variants be configured with lower concurrency by default? Pros: lowers regen cost; Cons: could increase latency.
- Are we comfortable with 120s stabilization across all heavy routes or only high-traffic ones?

Cheat sheet for noisy scenarios (one-line actions):
- High 5xx + scale loops -> increase stabilization window -> switch to fallback variant -> notify #prod-alerts.
- High latency + cache misses -> raise cache TTL -> trigger rewarm -> monitor p95.
- Node GPU warnings -> cordon -> drain -> replace if persists.

Last minute housekeeping before handing off:
- Drop a short note in #ops-shift-summary: current status + actions taken + items for morning. Example: "Flagfall done: switched text-gen-prod-v2->fallback @02:40 UTC, increased cache TTL for kv-cache-hotshot, cordoned node-3a for monitoring. Follow-ups: rewarm verification, node replacement. Aisha oncall next."
- Attach logs + screenshot of console graphs to JIRA-OPS-4312.

Personal quick reminders (notes to self):
- Pack spare noise-cancelling earbuds for night shift (I always forget).
- Remember to mute notifications from irrelevant channels when doing noisy remediation.

End of notes. Keep this doc minimal; the canonical runbook is at Confluence (linked above). If you expanded any temporary fixes into longer-term changes, update the linked JIRA and add a short blurb here for the next shift.

-- Jordan
